== Problem ==

A number <imath>N</imath> is inserted into the list <imath>2</imath>, <imath>6</imath>, <imath>7</imath>, <imath>7</imath>, <imath>28</imath>. The mean is now twice as great as the median. What is <imath>N</imath>?

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 7\qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 14\qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 20\qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 28\qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 34</imath>

== Solution 1 ==
We see the [[median]] is <imath>7</imath>. Since the mean is two times as great as the median, the mean must be <imath>7 \times 2 = 14</imath>. The sum of the numbers without <imath>N</imath> is <imath>2 + 6 + 7 + 7 + 28 = 8 + 14 + 28 = 50</imath>. Using the sum, we then have:

<imath>\frac{N + 50}{6} = 14</imath>. 

Multiplying both sides by <imath>6</imath>, we get:

<imath>N + 50 = 14 \times 6 = 84</imath>

<imath>N = 84 - 50 = \boxed{\text{(E)\ 34}}</imath>

~pereena and edited by anabel.disher four times

The median of the list is <imath>7</imath>, so the mean of the new list will be <imath>7 \cdot 2 = 14</imath>. Since there are <imath>6</imath> numbers in the new list, the sum of the <imath>6</imath> numbers will be <imath>14 \cdot 6 = 84</imath>. Therefore, <imath>2+6+7+7+28+N = 84 \implies N = \boxed{\text{(E)\ 34}}</imath>

~Soupboy0

==Solution 2==

Since the average right now is <imath>10</imath>, and the median is <imath>7</imath>, we see that <imath>N</imath> must be larger than <imath>10</imath>, which means that the median of the 6 resulting numbers should be <imath>7</imath>, making the mean of these <imath>14</imath>. We can do <imath>2 + 6 + 7 + 7 + 28 + N = 14 * 6 = 84</imath>. <imath>50 + N = 84</imath>, so <imath>N</imath> = <imath>\boxed{\text{(E)\ 34}}</imath>

~Sigmacuber

== Solution 4 ==

	
We could use answer choices to solve this problem. The sum of the <imath>5</imath> numbers is <imath>50</imath>. If you add <imath>7</imath> to the list, <imath>57</imath> is not divisible by <imath>6</imath>, therefore it will not work. Same thing applies to <imath>14</imath> and <imath>20</imath>. The only possible choices left are <imath>28</imath> and <imath>34</imath>. Now you check <imath>28</imath>. You see that <imath>28</imath> doesn't work because <imath>(28+50) \div 6 = 13</imath> and <imath>13</imath> is not twice of the median, which is still <imath>7</imath>. Therefore, only choice left is <imath>\boxed{\text{(E)\ 34}}</imath>

~ HydroMathGod

== Solution 5 ==

We see that in the list, both <imath>7</imath>s are <imath>3</imath>rd and <imath>4</imath>th. So, no matter what number we plug in, we will have two <imath>7</imath>s in <imath>3</imath>rd and <imath>4</imath>th. So, the median will always be <imath>7</imath>. That means we have to find the option that makes the mean <imath>14</imath>. If the mean is <imath>14</imath>, the sum of all the six numbers is <imath>84</imath>. The sum of the five numbers we are given is <imath>50</imath>, so the answer must be <imath>\boxed{\text{(E)\ 34}}</imath>

~ sdmd
